key_insight: Embedding graph-based turbine interactions into a Kriging surrogate improves sample-efficient Bayesian optimization of wind farm layouts.
engineering_relevance: The approach can reduce costly aerodynamic evaluations needed to design high-energy-yield wind farms, including large-scale CFD-based layouts.
method: Represent turbines and directed aerodynamic interactions as a graph.
Assemble low-dimensional pairwise interaction models into a farm-scale mean for annual energy production.
Use a Gaussian process to model residual structure and uncertainty within Bayesian optimization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports competitive IEA Wind Task 37 solutions with about 280 AEP evaluations, better performance than ordinary and multi-fidelity Kriging in a controlled 16-turbine case, and extension to 48 turbines.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how well reusable pairwise interactions capture the aerodynamics of new layouts and operating conditions.
paper_title: A Graph-informed Kriging model for sample-efficient Bayesian optimization of wind farm layouts
